No new modules; no changes outside write_paths.
residual_risks: iOS runtime behaviour (VoiceOver actually invoking increment/decrement, AppState transitions on device) is INFERRED from React Native's documented props and the existing StrokeResult scrubber; it is not provable from Linux and this package forbids running the Mac runner.
Native-driven playback (ClipPlayer present) is paused on backgrounding via the shared playing state that already drives the native `playing` prop; the JS-clock path is what the Jest suite exercises.
The coarser 120ms Reduce Motion tick applies only to the pose-only/JS-clock replay; native video playback cadence is the player's own.
implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA 55d80326 (VERIFIED by reading + by the failing regression run): apps/mobile/src/review/FormReviewPlayer.tsx lines 526-539 rendered the Form Review timeline as a plain `accessible` View with only a label/hint and touch responder handlers (seekToX/endScrub, lines 321-329). It had no accessibilityRole="adjustable", no accessibilityValue, no accessibilityActions and no onAccessibilityAction, so VoiceOver users could not seek at all (the only seek path was a finger drag). The player also had no AppState handling: a running replay (JS clock, lines 282-294; native ClipPlayer otherwise) kept its playing state when the app left the foreground. Reduced motion was honoured only by FormReviewOverlay's arrow entrance gate (FormReviewOverlay.tsx 245-265); the pose-only replay clock always ran at 30fps. By contrast the sibling replay scrubber in src/components/StrokeResult.tsx already had the adjustable role + increment/decrement pattern. Fix (apps/mobile/src/review/FormReviewPlayer.tsx only): the timeline View now carries accessibilityRole="adjustable", accessibilityValue {min 0, max durationMs, now playheadMs, text = clock + title of the stop under the playhead}, accessibilityActions [increment, decrement] and onSeekAccessibilityAction, which moves by durationMs/20 (clamped) through the existing jumpTo() so, exactly like a finger scrub, playback pauses, the native seek is requested and every checkpoint ahead is re-armed; unknown actions are ignored. A new AppState 'change' effect pauses playback whenever the app is not active (never auto-resumes; unsubscribes on unmount). With Reduce Motion on, the JS replay clock ticks every 120ms instead of every 33ms at the same wall-clock rate (auto-pause still freezes on the exact checkpoint frame). FormReviewOverlay.tsx was not modified: its reduced-motion arrow gate already behaves correctly and the new test pins it (Animated.timing not called, reducedMotion prop true). Regression test apps/mobile/__tests__/w09AccessibleSeek.test.tsx (6 tests) was committed first (919d7f3d) and fails 6/6 on BASE src; implementation commit ef72f078. All acceptance commands VERIFIED exit 0 on HEAD; additionally 11 related suites that render the player/result surfaces (resultGuide, savedTechniqueConfirmationRoute, resultRearmLoop, resultEvidenceAudit, coachLockAudit, strokeResultSurface, RootNavigator.buttons, flow-navigation-tabs-routes, ResultScreen.buttons, flow-analyze-result.result, analyzeScreenFullFlowE2E) pass 294/294 (https://la-hacks-rttothemoon.devinenterprise.com/attachments/4ab0f193-da04-4859-bdf9-f87e5e6049fc/related-suites.log).
